title: CHROMA: Conversational Human-Readable Optical Multilayer Assembly for Natural Language-Driven Inverse Design of Structural Coloration
experiments_summary: The study employs a multi-stage pipeline evaluated through a physics-first dataset construction and model scaling experiments. Dataset construction involves: (1) randomly generating multilayer thin-film stacks; (2) simulating their optical spectra using JaxLayerLumos on a 128-point wavelength grid from 380–780 nm; and (3) generating paired natural-language descriptions via templated prompts and paraphrasing techniques. The dataset comprises 72,000 training prompts (9,000 base structures × 8 templates) and 7,200 validation prompts (900 held-out base structures × 8 paraphrases). Two evaluation splits are used: a training-paraphrase (TP) split testing linguistic generalization on seen structures, and a held-out validation split testing inverse design on unseen optical targets. Model performance is evaluated using the CIE76 color difference metric (ΔE), computed by converting simulated reflectance spectra to tristimulus XYZ values via 1931 color-matching functions under a D65 illuminant, transforming to CIELAB space, and computing Euclidean distance. Scaling experiments systematically vary both the frozen Llama encoder size (1B vs. 8B parameters) and the trainable Transformer decoder depth (N = 2, 4, and 8 layers), plotting mean ΔE against the number of trainable parameters to assess how encoder scale and decoder depth independently affect performance on both evaluation splits. Qualitative analysis of successful and failure cases on the validation set is also performed to characterize model behavior under various constraint types (e.g., layer adjacency, ordering, thickness bounds, and layer count).
